name: TRIONFETTI
description: Trionfetti is a four-player partnership game from the rural area between Venice and Padua, played with an Italian suited 40- or 52-card deck. It is a relative of Truc and Put: the aim is to win at least two of three tricks per hand. The cutter (to dealer's left) freely chooses and announces the card ranking (comanda) for each smazzata; four consecutive hands are played from the same deck so players gain information across hands. First team to 20 points wins a game; first to 3 games wins the match.

It is a relative of Truc and Put: the aim is to win at least two of three tricks per hand. Trionfetti is a four-player partnership game from the rural area between Venice and Padua, played with an Italian suited deck (Trevigiane pattern). It was formally described by Alberto Fiorin at the IPCS Convention in 1997 and is the subject of a booklet by Gianluca Angi (2020). During the 1970s and 1980s several large tournaments were held; in 2009 the Club del 15 in Fossò founded the Scuola di Trionfetti, which still runs weekly meetings to teach new players. The game is a relative of Truc and Put and is preserved as a regional Venetian tradition.
40- or 52-card Italian deck (Trevigiane). Default ranking ascending: 1 (low) to King (high); 40-card lacks 8s, 9s, 10s.
Deal 3 cards each per hand. Same dealer deals up to 4 hands from the deck (smazzata). Cutter (to dealer's left) sees cut card and announces ranking (comanda) for the smazzata.
